      "file": "docs/audits/fixtures/metrics-uploader/uploader.py",

      "recommendation": "Replace the docstring claim with a reproducible measurement and document linear memory growth. If bounded memory is required, redesign batching to yield batches lazily and measure consumption without retaining them."

result.summary: Do not ship: batches exceed the API cap, the quota boundary is incorrectly accepted, and the memory claim is false. All five tests pass despite these defects.

findings.title: Batch size exceeds the API's 256-record cap
findings.body: BATCH_SIZE is 265 instead of 256. make_batches(range(257)) returns one 257-record batch; 1,000 records produce lengths [265, 265, 265, 205]. These violate the supplied API contract. Existing tests check batch counts and total records without checking each batch's size.
findings.recommendation: Set BATCH_SIZE to 256. Add boundary tests at 256 and 257 records that independently assert every batch is at most 256 and flattened output equals input.

findings.title: Floating-point rounding admits an exactly 10% reserve
findings.body: check_quota_split([0.3, 0.3, 0.3]) returns 0.10000000000000009 and accepts a nominal 90% allocation, violating the requirement that strictly more than 10% remain. The existing three-equal-shares test explicitly expects this incorrect acceptance. The guard also accepts NaN because its comparison is false.
findings.recommendation: Define decimal or fixed-unit quota semantics and enforce the threshold using that representation; reject non-finite inputs. Replace the equal-shares acceptance test with rejection and test reserves below, at, and above 10%.

findings.title: Recorded memory profile contradicts eager allocation
findings.body: The function materializes the entire input and every sliced batch simultaneously. A local tracemalloc run over 10 million repeated None records peaked at 162,423,160 bytes, contradicting both the under-4-MB figure and the claim that only one batch is held. Consumers relying on this profile can substantially underestimate memory requirements.
findings.recommendation: Replace the docstring claim with a reproducible measurement and document linear memory growth. If bounded memory is required, redesign batching to yield batches lazily and measure consumption without retaining them.

next_steps: Correct the cap and quota semantics, add regression tests, and replace the memory claim with measured evidence.
